title: Scanning beam
subtitle: Build a readable scanning beam with a reachable response and a useful recovery.
summary: A sustained beam sweeps across space from one side to another.
overview: A sustained beam sweeps across space from one side to another, turning a line hazard into a timed crossing or pacing challenge.
learning: Tune the signal, commitment, geometry, response, and recovery of a scanning beam as one rule.

demo.title: Test the scanning beam
phaseDescriptions: Reveal the pivot, sweep direction, start angle, and movement speed before activation so the player can plan where to cross.
Players can move ahead of the sweep, cross through a permitted gap, use cover, or rotate around the pivot at a safer radius.
The sweep pauses at its final angle and powers down before the pivot resets, avoiding an invisible damaging snap back to the start.

steps.title: Can the player read the complete rule?
steps.body: Reveal the pivot, sweep direction, start angle, and movement speed before activation so the player can plan where to cross.

steps.title: Is the intended response reachable?
steps.body: Players can move ahead of the sweep, cross through a permitted gap, use cover, or rotate around the pivot at a safer radius.

steps.title: Does recovery create a useful outcome?
steps.body: The sweep pauses at its final angle and powers down before the pivot resets, avoiding an invisible damaging snap back to the start.

mistakes.title: Changing sweep speed mid-attack without a cue invalidates the timing learned from the beam’s earlier movement
mistakes.body: Changing sweep speed mid-attack without a cue invalidates the timing learned from the beam’s earlier movement.

mistakes.title: The cue and active geometry disagree
mistakes.body: If the visible scanning beam cue promises a different area or timing, the player cannot carry the learned rule into the next cycle.

designNotes.title: Tune the complete rule
designNotes.body: Tune angular speed, beam width, pivot position, sweep range, and arena obstructions; test inner and outer routes separately.

designNotes.title: Escalate one variable at a time
designNotes.body: Reverse after a pause, move the pivot, or pair two scanners with offset timing while maintaining visible paths.

designNotes.title: Prove the recovery
designNotes.body: The sweep pauses at its final angle and powers down before the pivot resets, avoiding an invisible damaging snap back to the start.

story.title: What the mechanic communicates
story.body: A sustained beam sweeps across space from one side to another, turning a line hazard into a timed crossing or pacing challenge. The encounter uses that rule as a short promise: a visible signal, a committed action, and a result the player can verify.

adaptation.title: Adapt it to the player verbs
adaptation.body: Players can move ahead of the sweep, cross through a permitted gap, use cover, or rotate around the pivot at a safer radius. Tune angular speed, beam width, pivot position, sweep range, and arena obstructions; test inner and outer routes separately.

distinction.title: Keep the mechanic distinct
distinction.body: Changing sweep speed mid-attack without a cue invalidates the timing learned from the beam’s earlier movement. Do not hide that distinction behind extra effects or tracking that the announced rule does not contain.

lensNotes.body: The signal must reveal the relevant timing and geometry before commitment.
After commitment, the rule stops changing in ways the signal did not announce.
The complete player extent and the active region determine whether the route is real.
The response uses an ordinary supported verb and produces an observable result.
